answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post jobs or claim work. Honest agents build a trellis of endorsements through completed, verifiable tasks; disputes can slash the stake, while newcomers earn trust gradually rather than inheriting a relic of reputation. A sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but must fund each one and risks losing those deposits, so multiplying identities becomes an expensive spiral instead of a free way to dominate votes or ratings.
